one_liner: Embedded display driver and drawing library for ESP32-class MCUs; 1.3x to 4.6x faster than Adafruit_GFX on an ILI9341 at 40 MHz SPI.
what_it_does: LovyanGFX drives LCD, OLED and e-paper panels (ILI9341/9342, ST7735/7789/7796, GC9A01, SSD13xx, IT8951 and about 30 others) over SPI, I2C, 8/16-bit parallel, RGB and composite video, and draws primitives, bitmap/VLW/IPA/efont text, JPEG/PNG/QR images and off-screen sprites (1 to 24-bit, palette modes) with rotate/zoom. Drawing calls keep Adafruit_GFX and TFT_eSPI names (drawPixel, fillRect, drawCircle, setTextColor, print) and add arcs, ellipses, Bezier curves and gradient lines; LGFX_TFT_eSPI.hpp aliases TFT_eSPI and TFT_eSprite to LGFX so existing TFT_eSPI sketches can compile with few changes. Setup is different: you use an LGFX class from LGFX_AUTODETECT, a board define, or your own LGFX_Device subclass that wires a Bus (Bus_SPI, Bus_Parallel8 ...) to a Panel and optional Light and Touch, configured at run time.
how_it_is_fast: On ESP32 the Bus_SPI layer drives the SPI peripheral registers directly (MOSI_DLEN, W0-W15, CMD) and toggles D/C with one GPIO set/clear register write, skipping the Arduino SPI and ESP-IDF driver calls per transfer. Solid fills (writeDataRepeat) preload the 64-byte W0-W15 buffer with the colour and, on the original ESP32, retrigger 2048-bit transfers that reuse that buffer as a ring, so a fill runs at the link rate (Screen fill 154,341 us against a 153,600 us floor for five 240x320 RGB565 frames at 40 MHz, derived from page data). Pixel streams (writePixels) ping-pong between the W0-W7 and W8-W15 halves with SPI_USR_MOSI_HIGHPART so colour conversion overlaps the previous transfer. Panel_LCD caches the CASET/RASET window and skips resending it when unchanged; drawLine is Bresenham emitted as horizontal or vertical runs (writeFillRectPreclipped per run, with off-screen segments skipped before the bus is touched), and drawCircle is the midpoint algorithm emitted as eight H/V spans per step inside one held transaction.
when_to_use: Arduino or ESP-IDF firmware on ESP32, ESP32-S2/S3/C3/C6/P4 driving a supported SPI, I2C or parallel panel where Adafruit_GFX plus a controller driver is too slow: in the 2021 run it was 4.3x faster on text, 3.9x on lines and 3.3x to 4.6x on outline circles, triangles and rounded rectangles.

Shape-heavy screens (gauges, outlines, arcs): it was the fastest of the four libraries on 11 of 15 rows, and the only one besides Arduino_GFX with arc primitives (Arcs filled 21,546 us vs Arduino_GFX 33,381 us).

Products that must pick the board or panel at run time (LGFX_AUTODETECT for M5Stack, ODROID-GO, Wio Terminal and others), drive several displays at once, or use 24-bit colour, EPD panels or rotated and zoomed sprites (pushRotateZoom).
UI development on a desktop first: the same code renders through SDL2 or OpenCV on Windows, Linux or macOS (examples_for_PC) before flashing.
Moving an existing TFT_eSPI sketch onto a newer ESP32 core, via the LGFX_TFT_eSPI.hpp alias header.
when_not_to_use: Fill-dominated screens on SPI: fills are bound by the bus clock, so the gain over Adafruit_GFX is only 1.27x on Screen fill and 1.27-1.28x on filled rectangles and rounded rectangles at 40 MHz (derived from page data); a parallel bus or partial redraws matter more than the library.

Per-pixel plotting through drawPixel or text-heavy screens where every few percent counts: TFT_eSPI was 1.12x faster on Pixels (775,781 vs 867,702 us) and Arduino_GFX 1.19x faster on Text (18,960 vs 22,473 us) in the same run (derived from page data).
MCUs outside the README table: AVR, STM32 and nRF52 are not listed; RP2040 is SPI only with no touch support, and ESP8266 I2C is a software implementation.

Flash-tight targets on 1.2.30 or 1.2.31: merging the implementation into one translation unit kept unused panel and touch code and grew an ESP32-C3 build by about 575 KB (#940); 1.2.32 brings it back to 346 KB (1.2.29: 329 KB), so pin 1.2.32 or later and check the map file.
An SPI bus shared with devices in a different SPI mode on ESP32-S3: pinned open issue #491 reports a DAC in mode 2 stops responding after a display update, with no maintainer workaround posted.

integration.form: Arduino / PlatformIO library compiled from source (include LovyanGFX.hpp; v1 implementation in a few .cpp translation units since 1.2.32); ESP-IDF component and pico-sdk builds through CMakeLists.txt and boards.cmake
integration.dependencies: None outside the platform SDK for drawing; bundles TJpgDec, Pngle, QRCode and bitwizeshift/result; on ESP-IDF requires the nvs_flash, efuse, esp_lcd, driver and related components, and links an arduino-esp32 component automatically when present; SDL2 or OpenCV for PC builds
integration.min_toolchain: No language standard or core version is documented; CI badges cover Arduino IDE, PlatformIO and ESP-IDF builds, and the 1.2.32 release notes mention arduino-esp32 2.0.x and 3.0.x (ESP-IDF 5.1); PC builds use CMake 3.8+ with Clang or GCC
integration.platforms: ESP32, ESP32-S2, ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3 per the README table (SPI with DMA, I2C, parallel; RGB on S3; composite video on ESP32), plus ESP32-C6 and ESP32-P4 per recent commits (open issue #851: SPI DMA not working on ESP32-P4); ESP8266 (SPI), SAMD51/SAMD21 (SPI, I2C), RP2040 (SPI); Windows, Linux and macOS through SDL2 or OpenCV
integration.thread_safety: Not documented. startWrite/endWrite nesting is a plain uint32_t counter in IPanel and Panel_LCD tracks _in_transaction as a plain bool, so drive each LGFX object from one task; with use_lock = true (the Bus_SPI default) each transaction takes the ESP32 SPI bus lock so other devices on the bus are excluded while it runs.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: Adafruit_GFX-style drawing names and signatures work, and colour constants use TFT_* names, but the Adafruit_ILI9341(cs, dc, rst) constructor and begin(freq) are replaced by an LGFX class configured with Bus_SPI and Panel config structs (or autodetect), followed by init()

gotchas: The catalogued numbers were measured with the v0 API (lgfx::Panel_ILI9341 with public freq_write/spi_cs fields, setPanel, init(sclk, miso, mosi)); the run date points to tag 0.3.12 (2021-05-30), but the version was not recorded. v1 removed that API, so the benchmark sketch does not compile against current 1.2.x and the rewritten v1 code has not been re-measured.
Bus_SPI::config_t defaults freq_write to 16 MHz, not the 40 MHz the benchmark used; set it explicitly for ILI9341-class panels.

Colour arguments are typed by C++ type: uint32_t means RGB888, uint16_t and int32_t mean RGB565, uint8_t means RGB332. A bare literal like 0xFF0000 is an int and is read as RGB565; write 0xFF0000U for 24-bit colours.

draw* calls acquire and release the bus on every call (that is how the benchmark ran), while write* calls require an explicit startWrite(); holding startWrite() across a frame is faster but blocks other devices such as an SD card on the same SPI bus until endWrite() or endTransaction(). Before 1.2.32, pushImageDMA() with a source in PSRAM or flash sent garbage on ESP32 (#949).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick LovyanGFX over TFT_eSPI for the fastest shapes, fills and arcs on ESP32 SPI, run-time panel setup, ESP-IDF builds and current ESP32 chips (C6, P4, S3 RGB); TFT_eSPI kept a 12% lead on single pixels and a 1.5% lead on lines (the latter within the 7% spread between LovyanGFX's 2020 and 2021 runs) and has the STM32 and RP2040 PIO paths. Pick Arduino_GFX when you need its wider data-bus range or the fastest text; neither is comparable to Blend2D, Skia or AGG, which are desktop anti-aliased path rasterizers.
verified_claims_summary: One single-pass run of moononournation's Arduino_graphicstest_PDQ (2021-06-16; Arduino IDE 1.8.15, arduino-esp32 1.0.6, TTGO T8 v1.8 ESP32, PSRAM off, ILI9341 over 4-wire SPI at 40 MHz, no DMA; compiler flags, CPU clock and LovyanGFX version not recorded) timed the same test body per library: LovyanGFX beat Adafruit_GFX with Adafruit_ILI9341 by 4.6x on outline circles, 4.3x on text, 3.9x on lines, 3.7x on outline triangles, 1.6x on pixels and 1.27-1.3x on fills. The v0 code waits for the SPI busy flag in dc_h() before releasing the bus, so each timing includes the last transfer; the earlier 2020-10-15 run of the same suite gave LovyanGFX numbers up to 6.6% different (Pixels 814,232 vs 867,702 us).
status_note: Actively maintained: 2,008 commits, release 1.2.32 on 2026-10-02 fixing firmware size, ESP32-C6 builds and DMA from PSRAM, 16 open issues and no open pull requests; the main code is FreeBSD two-clause with MIT, BSD and IPA Font licences for bundled parts, so it is copyable.
